title: ide, oda, honnan, onnan: Here and There

sections.title: The itt/ott family, completed
sections.content: You know *itt* ("here") and *ott* ("there") for plain location, and from A1 you also know *ide* ("to here"), *oda* ("to there"), *innen* ("from here"), *onnan* ("from there") and *honnan* ("from where"). Here they come together as one set: *ide* and *oda* are the destination partners of *itt* and *ott*, and *innen* and *onnan* the starting-point partners, the same way *-hoz/-hez/-höz* and *-tól/-től* complete *-nál/-nél*.

sections.title: At / To / From, for here and there

sections.content: These sit in front of the verb as their own word, not glued on — *Ide jövök* and *Oda megyek* keep *ide*/*oda* separate, the same way you already write *nagyon szeretem* as two words.
